records.description: Initialize centres from a jittered staggered hex grid (random 5-7 rows, random subset of n points, jitter sd 0.02) instead of uniform random.
Pass SLSQP bounds (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.2]) and drop the redundant r>=0 constraint, keeping the wall constraints.

After random restarts for the first half of the time, repeatedly move the smallest circle of the best packing into the largest sampled hole, shrink radii by 5%, re-run SLSQP, and keep the result if the sum of radii improves.
Three-phase schedule (50% random restarts, 30% perturbing top-3, 20% long polish of best) with an analytic constraint Jacobian.
Run SLSQP in a 50-iteration first chunk, discard runs whose radius sum is below the 70th percentile of first-chunk results so far, and otherwise continue for the remaining iterations.
Add analytic constraint Jacobian, cut MAX_ITER to 100 and restart time to 70%, then polish the best packing with a 600-iteration SLSQP run.
Add analytic objective gradient and dense constraint Jacobian to SLSQP so each run is much faster and more restarts fit in the time budget.

issues: Integrity: clean. No file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

Correctness: no bug found. Elite entries are (sum, centers, radii) and the indexing matches. elite can't be empty at return because the first result is always inserted. Children still go through SLSQP, np.clip and _repair, so they can't produce an invalid packing. Timing is unchanged from the incumbent (stops at 80% of time_limit).

The harness's z = 0.001 doesn't match the given numbers: a 0.0001 difference over sd 0.0034*sqrt(2) gives z of about 0.021. The values are rounded to 4 decimals, so the exact z is uncertain, but the difference is noise either way and reject is the right decision.
The candidate adds about 30 lines (crossover plus an elite pool) for no measurable gain, which goes against 'simpler is better'.

Note, not the candidate's fault: the incumbent's 2.9375 is already above the card's 'best published' 2.9370. The usual published best for n=32 is about 2.9396, so the card's figure may be out of date.

records.description: Keep top 5 distinct packings and, in the last 30% of the time, seed SLSQP with children made from the left of parent A and the right of parent B at 0.9x radii.
Collect all restart results, refine the top 3 with trust-constr using an analytic Jacobian under a time deadline, re-solve the radii by LP, repair, and keep the best.
With probability 0.5 per restart (once a best exists), start SLSQP from the best centres plus noise sd 0.01 and 0.5 times the best radii, otherwise from the random hex init.
Draw initial radii uniformly from [0.03, 0.10] instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS, keeping the hex-grid centres.

Run random restarts for 60% of the time, then basin-hop from the best packing with global (sd 0.02) or local 4-circle (sd 0.08, every 5th try) perturbations and 0.8x radii, re-optimised by SLSQP with maxiter 150.
Build SLSQP pair constraints only for pairs initially closer than 0.35, then rerun with all pairs for 50 iterations if any pair overlaps.
Abort: basin hopping from the best packing after 60% restarts was already tried in slot 11 (+0.0020, noise-level), so it would repeat a failed schedule-style idea.
Run restarts with MAX_ITER 100, keep top 3 repaired candidates, and in the last 20% of the time polish each with SLSQP (maxiter 600, ftol 1e-12), keeping the best.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes the initial radii, and it draws them with the seeded rng, so there is no file access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The radii vector r0 has length n and its values are clipped to [0.02, 0.14], so x0 keeps its shape. The radii are sorted in descending order but the points are already randomly permuted, so the sort just pairs radii with points at random. That is harmless.
INIT_RADIUS may no longer be used anywhere after this change. It is dead code, a cosmetic problem only.

Recomputed z: (-2.9348 - (-2.9375)) / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) = 0.0027 / 0.00481 = +0.56 with the loss convention (candidate minus incumbent, positive means the candidate is worse). The harness reports -0.576, which is the opposite sign convention. Its magnitude is also slightly larger than the 0.551 to 0.572 that rounding the inputs to 4 decimals can explain. The harness may be using a slightly different sd. Either way the candidate is worse, and reject is the right decision.

Side note: the incumbent's single run, 2.9375, is slightly above the best published value of about 2.9370 stated on the card. That is plausible within noise and the harness checks every packing exactly, but the incumbent rests on only one run, so a replicate would make the baseline more reliable.
With n=1 on each side and z of about 0.56, the evidence is weak in both directions. The candidate does not show an improvement.

records.description: Start SLSQP from exponential-distributed initial radii (0.02 to 0.14), sorted descending and assigned to the jittered hex points, so a few big circles start first.
Diversify init: rows 4-8, jitter sd from {0.01,0.02,0.04}, random stagger 0 or 0.5, and 25% fully uniform random starts.
Half of the restarts reflect n//2 jittered hex-grid points across the diagonal to give a mirror-symmetric start (plus a diagonal point if n is odd).
Screen restarts with 60-iteration SLSQP for 50% of the time, then continue the top 15% from their saved x vectors with 300 iterations and return the best repaired packing.
Replace the hex-grid init with random row structures: k in {5,6,7} rows, circles split randomly among rows, evenly spaced in x with a random offset, evenly spaced y, small jitter.
Before SLSQP, relax the jittered hex-grid centres with 30 L-BFGS-B steps on a squared-overlap penalty at target radius 0.085 (pairs and walls, analytic gradient), then start SLSQP at radius 0.05.
Before SLSQP, relax centres and radii with L-BFGS-B on an analytic-gradient overlap penalty energy with mu increasing 10, 100, 1000.
Replace the regular hex grid init with R in 5-7 rows of random per-row counts (4-7, summing to n), each row randomly offset by half a spacing, with jitter sd 0.02.
Abort: the penalty pre-relaxation with L-BFGS-B was already tried in slot 20 (+0.0010) and slot 19 (-0.0020), both within noise.
Abort: two-stage screening with a continued top-pool is essentially what slots 17 (+0.0057) and 4 (+0.0000) already tried.

Keep a pool of the top 8 repaired packings and, with probability 0.5 per restart, seed SLSQP with a child made from the x<t circles of one parent and the x>=t circles of another (count fixed to n, radii shrunk).
Raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.92 and stop restarting when the remaining time is less than the longest single run seen so far.
Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.03 and TIME_FRACTION to 0.92 together.
Abort: irregular row layouts were already tried.
Use 85% of time for restarts, then 20 rounds of radius LP plus active-pair SLSQP polish on the best packing, keeping only improvements after repair.

After 70% of the time, repeatedly remove the smallest circle of the best packing, reinsert it at the largest sampled hole, re-run SLSQP (150 iterations), and keep the result if the repaired sum improves.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng. The change only alters the starting points: in 30% of restarts it builds a starting layout that is mirror-symmetric left to right. The existing SLSQP and repair steps still produce the final packing.

Recomputed z: (inc - cand) / (0.0034*sqrt(2)) = (-2.9375 + 2.9327) / 0.00481 = -0.998. This matches the harness value. Each side has only 1 run, so the result is not significant, but it points towards the candidate being worse (2.9327 vs 2.9375). Reject is reasonable.
Latent bug, not a veto: the symmetric branch returns 2*(n//2) points. For odd n that is n-1, and the shapes of x0 and the output would be wrong. It is harmless here because n=32.

Minor clutter: `* [1, 1]` does nothing. In the fallback, uniform points are drawn in [0.03, 0.47] for both coordinates, so y is limited to the bottom half. The fallback should never run for n=32 anyway.

Note: the incumbent's single run of 2.9375 is above the card's best published value of 2.9370. That is plausible within the 0.0034 noise, but the incumbent's mean rests on one run and may be optimistic. Rerunning the incumbent would make later comparisons more reliable.

records.description: With probability 0.3 per restart, start SLSQP from 16 jittered hex-grid points in the left half mirrored across x=0.5 plus sd 0.005 noise, otherwise the existing init.
In the second half of the time, restart SLSQP from the best centres plus log-uniform noise (sd 0.005 to 0.05) with radii reduced by 0.01, keeping the result if the repaired sum improves.
Abort: active-pair constraint pruning was already tried in slot 12 and hurt.
Abort: two-stage screening was already tried in slot 17 and hurt.

After 50% of the time on random restarts, spend the rest swapping the centres of two circles with different radii in the best packing, re-running SLSQP (150 iters) from there, and keep the result if the repaired sum improves.
Anneal the init jitter sd linearly from 0.04 to 0.01 over the restart time budget, keeping rows random 5-7.
Abort: swap-based neighbourhood search is essentially what slot 29 tried (+0.0044).
Abort: basin hopping from the best packing was already tried.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff only changes how starting centres are made: a hexagonal lattice with a random rotation and offset, trimmed to [0.03, 0.97], sampled down to n points and topped up with uniform points if too few survive. All randomness comes from rng, which is built from the seed. There is no file access, no pasted coordinates and no use of known answers. The existing SLSQP and repair steps still enforce validity.
No bug makes the result meaningless. The lattice spacing a = sqrt(2/(sqrt(3)(n+4))) is sensible, K is large enough to cover the square after rotation, and the fallback guarantees exactly n points.

Recomputed z: the difference is 2.9380 - 2.9375 = 0.0005 and the standard error is 0.0034*sqrt(1/1 + 1/1) ≈ 0.00481, so z ≈ 0.10. This matches the harness's 0.097, which probably used unrounded values (-2.938 is shown rounded).
The evidence is thin: 1 candidate run against 1 incumbent run. The gain is about 0.1 sd of noise, so it is not significant. Rejecting is correct unless replicates show a real gain.

Both values, about 2.9375 to 2.938, are above the 2.9370 quoted in the program card. They are still plausible because the best known value for n=32 is about 2.9379. The card's reference figure looks slightly low. This is not a sign of cheating.
Simplicity: the new seeding adds about 10 lines for a gain that may not exist. Under the 'simpler is better' rule this does not justify a change.

records.description: Initialise centres from a hex lattice with random rotation and offset (about n+4 points in the square), keep a random subset of n inside [0.03,0.97]^2, jitter sd 0.02.
Abort: irregular row-count init duplicates slots 18 and 21, which hurt.
With probability 0.5 per restart, start from n//2 jittered hex-grid points in the left half mirrored across x=0.5 (plus one point on x=0.5 if n is odd).

Before SLSQP, relax jittered hex-grid centres with 5 stages of L-BFGS-B (20 iters each) on an analytic-gradient squared-overlap penalty with common radius growing 0.04 to 0.095, then start SLSQP with radii 0.9 of the final scale.
Replace the iterative shrink repair with an exact LP for the radii at fixed centres (HiGHS), minus a 2e-7 safety margin, falling back to the old shrink if the LP fails.
Cycle the hex-init jitter sd through [0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.045] across restarts, keeping the 5-7 row choice.
Abort: mirror-symmetric init duplicates slot 32 (and slots 16 and 27), which hurt.
Run SLSQP first for 60 iterations with a 0.01 gap required between circles, then rerun from that result with no gap for the full MAX_ITER.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and the packing is still built by computation and passed through the existing _repair step. The final check is unchanged.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The LP in _kick is correct: r_i + r_j <= d_ij, and 0 <= r_i <= distance to the wall. If the LP fails, the code falls back to the old radii. The polished result is clipped and repaired before it is compared, and best is always set because the restart loop runs at least once. The new kick phase still stops at TIME_FRACTION * time_limit, so it adds no new risk of going over the time limit beyond the incumbent's existing one-iteration overrun.

Recomputed z: the gain is 2.9386 - 2.9375 = 0.0011. With one run on each side, se = 0.0034 * sqrt(2) ≈ 0.0048, so z ≈ 0.23. The harness reports 0.208, which matches a true gain of about 0.0010 before rounding. Both are far below any significance threshold, so 'reject' is the right provisional decision. Replicates would be needed to resolve a gain this small.

Minor: both means (2.9375 for the incumbent, 2.9386 for the candidate) are above the 'best published' value of about 2.9370 on the program card. This fits a known optimum of about 2.9379 plus noise with sd 0.0034, so it is not an integrity flag. The card's reference value may be slightly low.
Minor: the restart phase now uses a hard-coded 0.7 instead of a named constant. This is a small readability point, not a correctness issue.

records.description: After 70% of the time, repeatedly kick 3 centres of the best packing, re-solve radii with an exact LP, polish with 100-iteration SLSQP, and keep the result if the repaired sum improves.
Draw the init jitter sd log-uniformly in [0.005, 0.06] and the initial radius log-uniformly in [0.03, 0.08] per restart.
Abort: mirror-symmetric init was already tried in slots 16, 27 and 32.
After restarts, re-run SLSQP from the best raw solution with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-14, repair, and keep it only if the repaired sum improves.

memo:
Helped: only the init change in slot 0 (jittered staggered hex grid, 5-7 rows, random subset of positions): -2.9253 to -2.9375 (delta -0.0123), well above noise sd 0.0034. It is a single run, not yet replicated. Slots 6, 19 and 33 (-2.9396, delta -0.0020) are within noise, so they are possible but unconfirmed. Slot 31 (-0.0005) is noise.
Did not help: schedule edits (2-4, 7, 13, 23-25), bounds (1), analytic gradients alone (5), trust-constr polish (8), restarting from best or a pool (9, 11, 22, 28), random radii (10, 14), pair pruning (12), screening (17), swap moves (29), LP repair (34), and other hex-init variants (15, 16, 18, 21, 27, 32). These ranged from +0.0006 to +0.0087.
Next: replicate slot 0 once. Then combine it with slot 6 (analytic gradient and Jacobian) and slot 19 or 33 (L-BFGS-B pre-relaxation). Skip schedule and repair changes. Treat gains under 0.003 as noise.

incumbent.description: Initialize centres from a jittered staggered hex grid (random 5-7 rows, random subset of n points, jitter sd 0.02) instead of uniform random.

backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pairwise distance gradients, wall constraints, radius positivity) to minimize(). This speeds each SLSQP run by a large factor, giving many more restarts in the 24 s budget. Build the Jacobian as a dense array using the precomputed index arrays iu.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 500 and add ftol=1e-10 so that SLSQP converges fully to a local optimum rather than stopping early. Use together with analytic gradients if present.
backlog.title: Increase MAX_ITER to 500 with Jacobian

backlog.spec: After an initial phase of random restarts (about 40 percent of time), repeatedly take the best packing, perturb it (jitter all centres by sd 0.02 and shrink the radii by 20 percent, or relocate the 2-3 smallest circles to random positions), re-run SLSQP from it, and keep the result if it is better.
backlog.title: Basin hopping perturbation of best

backlog.spec: Initialize the centres from a jittered hexagonal or staggered grid layout (rows of 6/5 alternating, with random row counts and offsets) cropped to n points, rather than uniform random. Known good packings are near-hexagonal. Use random jitter of sd 0.02.
backlog.title: Hex-grid-like initialization

backlog.spec: Initialize the radii from a random distribution (uniform 0.03 to 0.10) instead of a constant 0.05, so the optimizer finds diverse radius distributions. Start from a feasible-ish state.
backlog.title: Mixed init: random radii

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 so initial states are feasible and SLSQP starts without large violations. Compare it with 0.05.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radius

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92. The repair step is cheap, and the limit is CPU time of 30 s with a 45 s hard void. Make sure the last restart cannot overrun: estimate the duration of a single run and stop if the remaining time is smaller.
backlog.title: Time fraction 0.92

backlog.spec: After the restarts, take the best raw solution and run SLSQP from it again with maxiter 1000 and ftol=1e-14 to squeeze out the final digits, then repair. Keep it only if the repaired sum is better.
backlog.title: Polish best with tight SLSQP

backlog.spec: Run many short SLSQP runs (maxiter 60), keep the top 10 percent by objective, and continue those with maxiter 500. This allocates compute to promising basins.
backlog.title: Two-stage restarts: short screening then long

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve the LP maximizing sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, using scipy linprog (highs), then subtract 1e-12 slack. This gives the optimal radii for those centres and is always valid, which replaces the iterative shrink.
backlog.title: Better repair: exact LP radii

backlog.spec: Restrict the pairwise constraints to pairs whose centre distance is below 0.35 at the start of each run and re-check after the solve. If any pair that was left out is violated, re-run with the full set. This shrinks the QP size of SLSQP and speeds each run.
backlog.title: Active-pair constraints only

backlog.spec: Write the non-overlap constraints as the squared distance minus (ri+rj)^2 >= 0. This is smooth at zero distance and has simpler Jacobians. Use with repair afterwards.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints

backlog.spec: Half of the restarts use initial centres that are mirror-symmetric about the diagonal (generate n/2 points and reflect them, adding points on the diagonal if n is odd). Best known packings are often near-symmetric. The optimizer is free to break the symmetry.
backlog.title: Seed with symmetric start

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of L-BFGS-B on the penalty energy -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2) with an increasing mu, starting from random points. Then run SLSQP from the result. This gives a better start than raw random points.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Local search: from the best solution, remove the smallest circle and put it at the largest empty hole (found by sampling 2000 random points and picking the one with maximum distance to the circle surfaces), shrink the radii slightly, then re-optimize with SLSQP. Accept if improved.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Choose initial centres with Lloyd relaxation (3 to 5 iterations on 5000 random samples in the square) so they are evenly spread, then set the radii to 0.4 times the nearest neighbour distance. Run SLSQP.
backlog.title: Initial radii from a Voronoi-like estimate

backlog.spec: Initialize with random row structures: choose the number of rows k in {5,6,7}, split the n circles among the rows at random, space them evenly in x within each row with a random offset, and use evenly spaced y values. Jitter slightly.
backlog.title: Vary circle counts of rows structured init

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in chunks of 50 iterations via warm restarts. After the first chunk, discard the run if the sum of radii is below the 70th percentile of the first-chunk results seen so far. Otherwise continue to convergence.
backlog.title: Early-reject poor runs

backlog.spec: For the top 3 solutions, refine with scipy trust-constr (with the analytic Jacobian), which is more accurate near degenerate active sets. After that, use the LP radii repair, and keep the best.
backlog.title: Trust-constr alternative at the end

backlog.spec: In the second half of the time, run SLSQP from the best-so-far centres plus Gaussian noise of sd drawn log-uniformly from 0.005 to 0.05, with the radii reduced by 0.01. Keep it if the repaired result is better.
backlog.title: Shake the centres with small noise on the best

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1], radii in [0, 0.2]. This removes the wall constraints on the centres, and the radius cap prevents runs from escaping to bad regions. Keep the wall constraints for c-r>=0.
backlog.title: Bounds on variables

backlog.spec: Replace the 50-iteration pair shrink by a vectorised loop that continues until no overlap exceeds 0 (up to 500 iterations) and use SHRINK=1e-12. This avoids losing sum of radii to the leftover violations or invalid packings. Verify with a final exact check.
backlog.title: Smaller repair shrink

backlog.spec: Initialize with a few big circles: sample the radii from an exponential-like distribution (0.02 to 0.14) sorted so that the large ones are placed on a coarse grid first and the small ones fill random positions. This steers the search towards packings with mixed sizes, which are typical of the best ones.
backlog.title: Large-radius-first start

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the top 8 solutions. Make a child by taking the circles of parent A with x<t and the circles of parent B with x>=t (random t, and fix the count to n by dropping or adding random circles), shrink the radii, and run SLSQP. Insert it into the pool if it is good.
backlog.title: Population with crossover of halves

backlog.spec: Reduce MAX_ITER to 100 together with analytic Jacobians so that more restarts fit. Then polish the top candidate with a long run. Tests the trade-off between iterations and restarts.
backlog.title: Lower MAX_ITER for more restarts

backlog.spec: Scale the objective to be -sum(r)*10 so that the SLSQP line search is better conditioned. Add a rescaling of the constraints by 10 too. Check that convergence is fine.
backlog.title: Log-barrier-free scaling of variables

backlog.spec: Initialize the centres on a perturbed 6x6 square grid with 4 random points removed, with the radii of 0.07, and noise sd 0.03. The square grid is a poor packing but it is a good start for rearrangement.
backlog.title: Targeted init near the best known structure type

backlog.spec: In every restart, with probability 0.5, start from the best solution's centres with the radii set to 0.5 times the best radii and noise sd 0.01, otherwise start from random. This mixes exploitation and exploration.
backlog.title: Warm-start from the best with the radius reset

backlog.spec: Identify the circle with the smallest radius in the best solution, and move it to a random location with radius 0.01 while shrinking the neighbours that overlap it. Re-run SLSQP for 100 iterations. Repeat for each of the 5 smallest circles in turn.
backlog.title: Sort-and-move the worst circle

backlog.spec: Divide the budget in three phases: 50 percent random restarts, 30 percent perturbation of the top 3 solutions, and 20 percent long polish of the best. Use the analytic Jacobian. Implement the phases with simple time checks.
backlog.title: Deterministic sorted multi-start by time slices

backlog.spec: Use 60% of the time for random restarts as now. Then, until the time is up, perturb the best packing: add Gaussian noise (sd 0.02) to all centres, set radii to 0.8 times the best radii, run SLSQP with maxiter 150, repair, and keep the result if it is better. Occasionally (every 5th try) perturb only the 4 circles nearest a random point with sd 0.08.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best packing

backlog.spec: After the restart phase, loop on the best solution. Pick two circles with different radii at random and swap their centres. Set radii to the mean radius for both, then re-optimize with SLSQP (maxiter 100). Repair and accept if the sum improves. This explores permutations of the size assignment that SLSQP cannot reach by itself.
backlog.title: Swap small and large circle positions

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw initial radii from a uniform distribution on [0.03, 0.10] instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS. Keep the hex-grid centres. The size diversity may help find solutions with mixed big and small circles, which are typical of the best packings.
backlog.title: Random-radii hex init

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run 30 steps of gradient descent on the centres. The energy is the sum of squared overlaps at a target radius of 0.085 (pairs and walls). Use L-BFGS-B with an analytic gradient. This spreads the circles uniformly. Then start SLSQP from these centres with initial radius 0.05.
backlog.title: Penalty pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Make the init family broader. Choose rows R from 4..8 at random. Choose the jitter sd from {0.01, 0.02, 0.04}. With probability 0.25 use a fully uniform random start of centres instead. Also draw the row offset (stagger) randomly from {0, 0.5}. This keeps the init simple but diversifies the basins.
backlog.title: Row-count and jitter sweep

backlog.spec: Run each restart with MAX_ITER 100. Then fully polish only the top 3 candidates, ranked by repaired sum. The polish is SLSQP with maxiter 600, ftol 1e-12, started from the candidate (centres and radii). Keep a list of the top 3 during the restart phase and reserve the last 20% of the time for the polish.
backlog.title: Staged SLSQP with tighter polish

backlog.spec: With probability 0.3 per restart, build a start that is symmetric: generate n/2 points in the left half (x<0.5) from the jittered hex pattern and reflect them to x -> 1-x. If n is odd, add a point on x=0.5. Add small noise (0.005) to break the exact symmetry. Many good packings are near-symmetric, so this seeds that structure.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric init

backlog.spec: Change the pair constraints to (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance. Provide the analytic sparse-free Jacobian over the pair index arrays via jac=. Use it in SLSQP, and keep the wall and r>=0 constraints linear. The cheaper, smoother evaluations should allow more restarts in the same time.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct packings during restarts. In the last 30% of the time, build children as follows. Take the circles of parent A with x<t (t random in 0.35..0.65) and the circles of parent B with x>=t. Fix the count to n by dropping the smallest circles or adding random points. Set radii to 0.9 times the parent radii, run SLSQP, and repair. Insert the child into the elite set if it beats the worst member.
backlog.title: Elite recombination of halves

backlog.spec: Replace _repair with a linear program: keep centres fixed and solve for radii maximizing sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= distance to walls, r >= 0, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Then subtract SHRINK (1e-9) and run the existing pairwise check, shrinking any remaining violating pair so the result stays valid. Apply it to every restart result and to the final best. This recovers the radius sum lost by the greedy shrinking.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius repair

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, build the pair constraints only for pairs whose initial centre distance is below 0.35, instead of all 496 pairs. Then run SLSQP on that set. After it finishes, check all pairs, and if any pair is violated, rerun SLSQP from the result with the full pair set for 50 iterations. Each run becomes much cheaper, so more restarts fit into the time limit.
backlog.title: Active-pair constraints with neighbour list

backlog.spec: After 60% of the time spent on random restarts, switch to basin hopping from the best packing. Each step picks 1-3 random circles, relocates them to random positions (or swaps two circles of different radii), adds Gaussian noise of sd 0.01 to all centres, and sets radii to 0.8 times their old value. Run SLSQP for 100 iterations from this point and accept the result if its repaired sum is larger. Use the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Basin hopping on the best packing

backlog.spec: Change init so that the radii start with a bimodal pattern: pick a random 20-30% of the circles as large (radius 0.09) and the rest small (radius 0.05). Keep the jittered staggered hex centres. Optimal packings of this kind contain circles of mixed sizes, so this seeds the right structure.
backlog.title: Mixed-size hex init

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a cheap stage of 30-50 L-BFGS-B iterations on a smooth penalty: -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2) + wall violations squared, with analytic gradients and mu = 50. Then pass the result to SLSQP, with radii scaled by 0.95 so it starts near a feasible point. This spreads the circles before the expensive solve.
backlog.title: Penalty pre-relaxation stage

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform R x m hex layout with rows that have varying counts. Choose a row count R from 5 to 7, and give each row a count from {4,5,6,7} so the total is exactly 32. Space the rows evenly in y and the circles evenly in x in each row, with a random half-offset. Add jitter of sd 0.015. This covers more of the layout families found in best known packings.
backlog.title: Row layout sweep with irregular rows

backlog.spec: For each restart, run SLSQP for 60 iterations and compute the radius sum of the repaired result. Keep a pool of the top 4 intermediate states. For the last 40% of the time, continue the pool members with another 300 SLSQP iterations each, round-robin. Return the best final repaired packing. This allocates the budget to promising basins.
backlog.title: Two-stage screening with a bounded SLSQP budget

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, build the starting centres by generating 16 random hex-jittered points in the left half (x<0.5) and mirroring them to x -> 1-x to make 32. Do not impose symmetry on the optimizer. SLSQP will then break it when that is favourable. Symmetric starts often lead to good packings.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric init

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 10% of the time. Take the best packing and run SLSQP with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=1000 from it, using the radii scaled by 0.999. Repair the result and keep it only if its sum is larger than the best.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish of the best

backlog.spec: Make the jitter sd in the init a random log-uniform value in [0.005, 0.06] per restart instead of the fixed 0.02. Also draw INIT_RADIUS log-uniformly in [0.03, 0.08]. Keep a record of the best runs. This diversifies the starts so that the search covers more basins.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted jitter by annealed restarts

backlog.spec: After the restarts end (use the last 25% of the time), take the best packing. Loop: solve the radius LP for fixed centres with linprog. Then move centres a small step along the LP dual-weighted gradient of the active constraints, or run SLSQP from the current point with MAX_ITER 300 and tight ftol=1e-15. Keep the result only if the repaired sum improves. This pushes the best basin to its exact local optimum.
backlog.title: Alternating LP and centre-gradient polish of best

backlog.spec: In the last 30% of the time, take the best packing. Each iteration picks two circles with clearly different radii, swaps their centres, scales the radii to the new sites (or resets all radii to 0.8 of their values), and runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER 150. Accept if the repaired sum is larger. Use rng for the choice. This is a discrete swap move, different from the perturbation and basin-hopping moves already tried.
backlog.title: Swap-based neighbourhood search on best

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in _solve_once, run about 100 steps of L-BFGS-B (or plain gradient descent) on the penalty energy: sum of squared overlaps of pairs and walls, with radii equal to a common scale s that grows from 0.04 to 0.095 in stages. Start SLSQP from the relaxed centres with the radii set to 0.9 of the relaxed radii. This gives well-spread feasible-ish starts. Vectorize with numpy on the pair index arrays.
backlog.title: Penalty pre-relaxation with growing radii

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, build the start from a hex grid with 5-6 rows as now. Choose about 4 random circles to be big, and set their initial radii to 0.12 and all other radii to 0.07. Put the big circles near random grid points. Known good packings of this kind have a few large circles among smaller ones, so this should favor those. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Mixed-size hex init

backlog.spec: Generate 16 jittered hex-grid points in the left half (x<0.5), mirror them across x=0.5 to get 32 points, and add small noise of sd 0.005 to break the exact symmetry. Use this as the start for SLSQP with probability 0.3 per restart, and the existing init otherwise. Optimal packings are often near-symmetric, so this searches that subspace.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric start

backlog.spec: Change the pair constraint in cons from sqrt distance minus r_i minus r_j to the smooth form d2 - (r_i + r_j)**2 where d2 is the squared distance. Keep the wall constraints the same. This avoids the sqrt singularity at zero distance and gives SLSQP a smoother problem. Because r_i + r_j >= 0 it is equivalent to the original constraint. Add the analytic Jacobian if simple, otherwise rely on finite differences.
backlog.title: Square-root-free squared-distance constraints

backlog.spec: Run each restart with MAX_ITER 60 and record the sum of radii after a quick repair. Collect the candidates in a list. Spend the first 50% of the time on screening. Then take the top 15% of candidates by sum, continue each from its saved SLSQP state (x vector) with MAX_ITER 300, and return the best. Implement by storing the raw x vectors and calling minimize again from them.
backlog.title: Two-stage screen with variable budget

backlog.spec: Replace the regular grid in _solve_once. Pick R in 5-7 rows, and draw per-row counts that sum to 32, each between 4 and 7, by random choice. Place each row's centres evenly across x with a random offset of half a spacing, at y=(i+0.5)/R, then add jitter sd 0.02. This varies the structure type far more than a fixed-shape grid. Everything else stays as is.
backlog.title: Row layouts with irregular row counts

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in two phases. Phase 1 maximizes sum of r minus 0.5 times the sum of the squared radii deviations from their mean, with MAX_ITER 60. This is a regularizer that keeps the radii balanced and avoids early collapse of small circles. Phase 2 starts from the phase 1 result and maximizes the plain sum of r with MAX_ITER 150. Report the phase 2 result.
backlog.title: Soft-start constraint weighting via two-phase radius target

backlog.spec: After restarts (use 85% of time for them), take the best packing and run 20 rounds: (a) solve the radius LP for fixed centres, (b) run SLSQP from that point with maxiter 50 on only active pairs (distance - r_i - r_j < 0.02) plus wall constraints. Keep the result only if the repaired sum improves. Final result goes through the LP repair.
backlog.title: Alternating LP and centre-gradient polish of best

backlog.spec: For half of the restarts, generate n//2 jittered hex-grid points in the left half of the square (x<0.5), mirror them across x=0.5 to give pairs, and if n is odd add one point on x=0.5. Add small independent noise (sd 0.005) to break exact symmetry, then run SLSQP as usual. The other half of the restarts use the existing init.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric init

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, pick R in 5..7 rows, but give each row a different count of circles (sample counts that sum to n=32, each between 4 and 7), spaced evenly in x with a random half-step offset per row. Jitter with sd 0.02 and run SLSQP. Keep everything else identical to the slot 0 init.
backlog.title: Irregular row counts hex init

backlog.spec: After 70% of the time on restarts, loop: take the best packing, swap the centres of two circles with different radii (chosen at random from neighbouring pairs), reset radii to 0.8 of their current value, run SLSQP with maxiter 100, and accept if the repaired sum improves. Run until time is used.
backlog.title: Swap-based neighbourhood search on best

backlog.spec: After 70% of the time, take the best packing, delete the smallest circle, estimate the largest hole by evaluating a 60x60 grid of points for max distance-to-nearest-surface (distance to circles minus radius, and wall distance), place the circle there with radius half that value, then run SLSQP maxiter 150. Repeat with the 2nd and 3rd smallest circles too. Accept improvements only.
backlog.title: Remove and reinsert smallest circle in largest hole

backlog.spec: Reformulate the SLSQP pair constraints as (dx^2+dy^2) - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0 with an analytic sparse-free dense Jacobian, also add r_i+r_j >= 0 implicit via r>=0. This removes the sqrt singularity and speeds each iteration, permitting more restarts. Final validity is still guaranteed by the repair step.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian

backlog.spec: Keep top 6 distinct repaired packings from the first 60% of time. In the remaining time create children: pick two parents, take circles of parent A with x<t (t random in 0.35..0.65) and circles of parent B with x>=t, adjusting to exactly n by dropping or adding random-position circles with small radii. Run SLSQP maxiter 200 from the child, and add the result to the elite pool if good.
backlog.title: Elite crossover of halves

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.03 and TIME_FRACTION to 0.92 simultaneously. A smaller start lets SLSQP grow circles from a feasible state, and more restarts use the available CPU. Keep the repair at the end so the time overrun stays safe (restart runs take about 0.3 s).
backlog.title: Smaller initial radius and time fraction 0.92

backlog.spec: Make the init jitter sd decrease across restarts: sd = 0.04 at the start going linearly to 0.01 at the end of the time budget, with the row count still random 5-7. Early restarts explore widely and later ones stay near hex structure. One change only.
backlog.title: Annealed-jitter restarts

backlog.spec: Keep the current train.py unchanged except add a constant SEED_OFFSET = 0 used as np.random.default_rng(seed + SEED_OFFSET). Purpose: measure the real mean of the hex-init baseline. Run it once to see whether -2.9375 is reproducible and to calibrate noise before further changes.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 0 baseline with seed offset

backlog.spec: Replace _repair with: clip centres to [0,1], then solve the linear program max sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= distance to walls, r>=0 using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Then subtract SHRINK 1e-10 from the radii and clip at 0. This recovers radius lost by the greedy shrinking. Verify validity by a final pairwise check; if any pair violates, fall back to the old repair.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius repair after SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, with probability 0.5 build the start from n//2 jittered hex-grid points in the left half (x<0.5), mirror them across x=0.5, and add a centre-line circle if n is odd. Otherwise use the normal init. SLSQP runs on all variables and may break the symmetry. Draw the half-points by the same staggered grid restricted to x<0.5.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric init

backlog.spec: Rewrite the pair constraints in SLSQP as (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance. Supply an analytic dense Jacobian for all constraints. Keep MAX_ITER 200 and the hex init. The repair step still guarantees validity. Test whether the smoother constraints give better local optima.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with analytic Jacobian

backlog.spec: Make the jitter sd of the hex init vary with the restart index, cycling through [0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.045] in sequence, while keeping the 5-7 row choice. Differs from slot 15 by changing only jitter and keeping stagger and rows as in slot 0.
backlog.title: Annealed jitter across restarts

backlog.spec: After 70% of the time, take the best packing and repeat: remove the smallest-radius circle, find the largest empty hole by sampling 20000 random points and picking the one maximizing min(distance to other circles minus their radii, wall distance), put the circle there with a small radius, run SLSQP (MAX_ITER 150) and accept if the repaired sum improves. Use the remaining time for this loop.
backlog.title: Remove worst circle and reinsert into largest hole

backlog.spec: Keep MAX_ITER=200 for restarts, and store the top 3 raw (unrepaired) results. In the final 15% of the time, rerun SLSQP from each with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-12, then repair and keep the best. Raw results must be stored before repair.
backlog.title: Bigger MAX_ITER on top candidates only

backlog.spec: Phase 1: run SLSQP for 60 iterations with all radii tied to a single shared value via the objective -sum r plus the constraint set, using start radius 0.05. Phase 2: continue from the result with free radii for the remaining iterations (up to MAX_ITER 200). Use the hex init. This gives an equal-circle-like start before breaking size symmetry.
backlog.title: Two-phase SLSQP with radius target

backlog.spec: Make no change to the current train.py (the jittered hex-grid init is already in place). Run it once more purely to measure the true baseline of the incumbent against noise sd 0.0034. This calibrates every later comparison.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 0 baseline

backlog.spec: Add an analytic objective gradient (-1 on radii entries) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian for the pair, wall and r>=0 constraints in _solve_once, passed via jac= in minimize. Raise MAX_ITER to 300 so that each SLSQP run converges more fully. Keep TIME_FRACTION and the init unchanged. This combines slot 6 (-2.9396) with the incumbent init and gives deeper convergence per run.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian plus hex-grid init, MAX_ITER 300

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in _solve_once, run scipy L-BFGS-B for 30 iterations on the centres only (radii fixed at INIT_RADIUS) to minimise the sum of squared pair overlaps plus squared wall violations, using an analytic gradient. Then start SLSQP from the relaxed centres. This repeats slot 19 (-2.9396), which was within noise, so run it again to see if it is real.
backlog.title: Pre-relax with L-BFGS-B on hex init, 30 steps

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, build the initial centres by generating n//2 jittered hex-grid points in the left half of the square (x<0.5) and mirroring them across x=0.5. If n is odd, add one point on x=0.5. Use the usual INIT_RADIUS and let SLSQP break the symmetry freely. This gives a different family of starts than the diagonal reflection of slot 16.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric init

backlog.spec: Make the init a hex lattice with a random rotation angle in [0, 60 degrees) and a random offset. Choose the lattice spacing so that about n+4 points fall in the unit square, keep a random subset of n points inside [0.03, 0.97]^2, and add jitter sd 0.02. This varies the lattice orientation, which the row-based init cannot do, while keeping the near-hex density that worked.
backlog.title: Hex lattice with a rotated random orientation and clipping

backlog.spec: Reformulate the pair constraints as (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance and cheap, and give an analytic Jacobian. Keep the wall constraints. Keep everything else the same. The smoother constraints may let SLSQP converge in fewer iterations and allow more restarts in the time budget.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian

backlog.spec: Sample the number of hex rows R from {5,6,7} with weights tuned by adaptive bandit: keep a running mean of final radius sum per R value and sample R with softmax probability (temperature 0.005) after 10 restarts have been done. Before that, sample uniformly. This concentrates the budget on the row counts that actually give better packings.
backlog.title: Two-level time schedule on radius-count-aware init

backlog.spec: In the last 25% of the time, take the best packing, multiply each radius by a random factor in [0.6, 1.0] and add centre noise of sd 0.005 to only the 5 circles with smallest radii, then run SLSQP from there with MAX_ITER 200. Accept if the repaired sum improves. This is a small local kick aimed at the weakest circles, unlike the earlier global basin hops.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-reoptimise radii-only kick on best

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP objective use -sum(r) - lam * sum(log(r + 0.01)) with lam = 0.002 with random restarts, to discourage tiny circles early. Run a second short SLSQP (50 iterations) from the result with the pure -sum(r) objective. This regularisation shapes the landscape in the first stage and then recovers the true objective.
backlog.title: Weight the objective with a decaying penalty for small radii

backlog.spec: Keep train.py exactly as the current incumbent (jittered hex init) but change the rng seed to np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000). Purpose: measure how much of the -2.9375 is real versus lucky; no other change.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 0 baseline with different seed offset

backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and a dense analytic Jacobian for cons (pair rows: derivative of distance wrt both centres and -1 for both radii; wall rows; identity for r>=0). Raise MAX_ITER to 300 so each SLSQP converges further. Keep the hex init and the 0.8 time fraction.
backlog.title: Analytic gradient and Jacobian plus hex init with MAX_ITER 300

backlog.spec: Replace the pair constraint sqrt(d2)-ri-rj>=0 by a smooth form: d2-(ri+rj)^2>=0 with analytic Jacobian (2*(ci-cj) for centres, -2*(ri+rj) for radii). Avoids the sqrt singularity and speeds up SLSQP, allowing more restarts. Keep the final _repair for exactness.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian

backlog.spec: For each restart, set initial radii from a bimodal draw: about 4 randomly chosen circles start at 0.11 and the rest at 0.05, while the centres come from the hex-grid init as now. Known good packings of 32 circles contain several distinctly larger circles; this seeds that structure.
backlog.title: Mixed-size hex init with a few big circles

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, generate 16 jittered hex-grid points in the left half (x<0.5) and mirror them across x=0.5 to get 32 centres, with the initial radii copied from the mirrored partner. SLSQP then runs unconstrained by symmetry so it can break it.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric init

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 10% of time (restarts stop at 0.7 of the limit). Take the best packing before repair and run SLSQP from it with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-14, then repair. Keep the result only if the repaired sum is larger.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: Run each SLSQP in two phases: the first phase with the objective plus constraint cons shifted to require a gap of 0.01 between circles (d - ri - rj >= 0.01) for 60 iterations, then the second phase with the gap removed, started from the phase-one result. The gap spreads circles evenly before the tight optimisation.
backlog.title: Squeeze-and-regrow radius schedule

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add a random horizontal phase offset in [0,1) cells to every row independently (not only the 0.5 stagger), and draw R from 5-7 as now. This yields dislocated lattice defects that the current regular rows never produce. Keep jitter sd 0.02.
backlog.title: Larger row-offset shift hex init with random column phase

backlog.spec: After 70% of the time, repeatedly take the best packing, perturb 3 random circle centres by N(0,0.05), solve the exact radius LP (scipy linprog, maximise sum of radii subject to pairwise ri+rj<=dij and wall limits), then run SLSQP with maxiter 100 from there. Accept if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Radius-only LP kick on best

backlog.spec: In the first SLSQP call per restart, use the objective -sum(w*r) with w=1+0.5*(r_mean-r)/r_mean recomputed from the starting radii (so smaller circles are favoured), for 80 iterations. Then finish with the plain objective for the remaining iterations. This encourages equalised radii before the final tuning.
backlog.title: Decaying small-radius weight in objective
